name: OpenCompany PR triage and merge

args.script:
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/enamakel/work/tinyhumansai/workflow-opencompany
BATCH=${OC_TRIAGE_BATCH:-5}
cd "$ROOT"

# Scoped to the opencompany repository only: the operator asked for its PRs and
# not the sibling submodules (backend, openhuman, dashboard, k8s, landing,
# opencompany-microservice) or the superproject itself. `origin` is often a
# personal fork; prefer `upstream` where it exists, because that is where the
# PRs live.
dirs="opencompany"
all=$(mktemp)
warn=$(mktemp)
: > "$all"

for d in $dirs; do
  url=$(git -C "$d" remote get-url upstream 2>/dev/null || git -C "$d" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null) || continue
  slug=$(printf '%s' "$url" | sed 's#.*github.com[:/]##; s#\.git$##')
  # Deliberately NOT asking for statusCheckRollup here: on a repo with dozens of
  # open PRs GitHub's GraphQL endpoint answers with a 504 every time. Check
  # state is fetched per PR below, only for the ones that could still merge.
  raw=$(gh pr list -R "$slug" --state open --limit 100 \
        --json number,title,url,isDraft,author,updatedAt,headRefName,mergeable,reviewDecision 2>/dev/null) || {
    printf -- '- could not list %s\n' "$slug" >> "$warn"; continue; }
  printf '%s' "$raw" | jq --arg slug "$slug" --arg dir "$d" '[ .[] | select(.isDraft | not) | {
        repo: $slug, dir: $dir, number, title, url,
        author: (.author.login // "?"), branch: .headRefName,
        updated: (.updatedAt | split("T")[0]),
        mergeable: (.mergeable // "UNKNOWN"),
        reviewDecision: (if (.reviewDecision // "") == "" then "NONE" else .reviewDecision end)
      } ]' >> "$all"
done

# Probe CI only where it can still change the answer, so the run costs a
# handful of calls rather than one oversized query per repository.
cand=$(jq -s '[ .[] | .[] ] | unique_by(.repo + "#" + (.number|tostring)) | sort_by(.updated) | reverse' "$all")
probed=$(printf '%s' "$cand" | jq -c '.[]' | while read -r pr; do
  slug=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r .repo); n=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r .number)
  m=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r .mergeable); rd=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r .reviewDecision)
  if [ "$m" != "MERGEABLE" ] || [ "$rd" = "CHANGES_REQUESTED" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -c '. + {failing: [], pending: [], checks: "unprobed"}'; continue
  fi
  roll=$(gh pr view "$n" -R "$slug" --json statusCheckRollup 2>/dev/null) || roll='{"statusCheckRollup":null}'
  printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -c --argjson r "$roll" '. + {
      failing: [ ($r.statusCheckRollup // [])[] | select(((.conclusion // .state // "")|ascii_upcase) | test("FAILURE|TIMED_OUT|CANCELLED|ERROR")) | (.name // .context // "check") ],
      pending: [ ($r.statusCheckRollup // [])[] | select(((.conclusion // .state // "")|ascii_upcase) | test("^$|PENDING|IN_PROGRESS|QUEUED")) | (.name // .context // "check") ],
      checks: "probed" }'
done | jq -s '.')

# Everything a command can decide is decided here, so a harness session is only
# spent on PRs that could actually merge.
printf '%s' "$probed" | jq --argjson batch "$BATCH" --rawfile warnings "$warn" '
  def ready: .mergeable == "MERGEABLE"
             and (.failing | length) == 0
             and (.pending | length) == 0
             and .reviewDecision != "CHANGES_REQUESTED";
  def line: "- " + .repo + "#" + (.number|tostring) + " by " + .author
            + " (updated " + .updated + ", review " + .reviewDecision + ") " + .title
            + "\n  " + .url + "\n  local checkout: " + .dir;
  { total: length,
    eligible: [ .[] | select(ready) ],
    blocked:  [ .[] | select(ready | not) ] }
  | . + { candidates: (.eligible[0:$batch]) }
  | . + { count: (.candidates | length),
          deferred: ((.eligible | length) - (.candidates | length)) }
  | . + { report:
      ( "Open non-draft PRs found in tinyhumansai/opencompany: " + (.total|tostring)
        + "; eligible to review: " + (.eligible|length|tostring)
        + "; in this batch: " + (.count|tostring)
        + "; deferred to a later run: " + (.deferred|tostring) + "\n\n"
        + (if ($warnings | length) > 0 then "Repositories that could not be listed this run:\n" + $warnings + "\n" else "" end)
        + "REVIEW THESE, AND ONLY THESE:\n"
        + ([ .candidates[] | line ] | join("\n"))
        + "\n\nNot in scope this run (conflicting, red or pending checks, or changes requested):\n"
        + ([ .blocked[] | line + "\n  mergeable=" + .mergeable
             + " failing=" + (if .checks == "unprobed" then "unprobed" elif (.failing|length) == 0 then "none" else (.failing|join(",")) end)
             + " pending=" + (if .checks == "unprobed" then "unprobed" elif (.pending|length) == 0 then "none" else (.pending|join(",")) end) ] | join("\n")) ) }'
rm -f "$all" "$warn"

nodes.name: Review the batch and merge what passes

config.prompt:
=("You are triaging pull requests for the tinyhumansai/opencompany repository, checked out at /Users/enamakel/work/tinyhumansai/workflow-opencompany/opencompany. Only PRs in that repository are in scope this run; ignore the sibling submodules and the superproject even if you notice open PRs there.

For each PR in the list below, in order:
1. Read it with `gh pr view <n> -R <repo>` and `gh pr diff <n> -R <repo>`, plus its review threads and CI conclusions.
2. Review it properly: does the diff do what the title and body claim, is it scoped to one change, does it touch secrets, credentials, destructive migrations, or CI/release plumbing, does it break a public interface, and does it have tests where the repo expects them?
3. MERGE it with `gh pr merge <n> -R <repo> --squash` only when all of these hold: the review found nothing that needs changing, checks are green, no unresolved review thread asks for a change, and the base branch is that repository's default branch.
4. Otherwise DO NOT MERGE. Leave one review comment on the PR naming precisely what blocks it, and move on.

Rules: touch only the PRs listed below. Do not push commits, do not amend anyone's branch, do not commit anything in the operator's local checkouts, and do not close a PR. Prefer reading the PR through `gh` over mutating any working tree. If you run out of time, stop cleanly and report the PRs you did not reach.

Finish with one line per PR: `<repo>#<number> MERGED` or `<repo>#<number> SKIPPED — <one-line reason>`.

" + .nodes.collect.item.json.output.report)

args.script:
set -uo pipefail
# Ask GitHub what happened rather than trusting the session's own summary.
#
# Never swallow gh's own stderr here. The 2026-07-30 run merged #196, #195 and
# #193 and still reported every one of them as UNKNOWN, in 109ms for three
# network calls — i.e. gh failed instantly (missing binary, missing auth, or a
# 403) and the discarded stderr was the only thing that said which. A bare
# UNKNOWN beside a real merge is indistinguishable from a PR genuinely in limbo,
# so print the reason next to it.
jq -r '.[]? | .repo + " " + (.number|tostring)' | while read -r slug n; do
  err=$(mktemp)
  state=$(gh pr view "$n" -R "$slug" --json state --jq .state </dev/null 2>"$err") || state=""
  if [ -n "$state" ]; then
    printf -- '- %s#%s -> %s\n' "$slug" "$n" "$state"
  else
    printf -- '- %s#%s -> UNKNOWN (gh: %s)\n' "$slug" "$n" "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$err" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
  fi
  rm -f "$err"
done

description: Survey every open PR across the workflow-opencompany superproject and its submodules, deterministically drop the ones that cannot merge, then review a batch of the eligible ones on a harness and merge the ones that pass review.
